title: Vertical Line Test - GeeksforGeeks

Vertical Line Test is a simple method used in mathematics to determine whether a given graph represents a function. The test involves drawing a vertical line through different points on the graph. If at any point the line intersects the graph more than once, the graph does not represent a function.

This is because a function has only one output (y-value) for each input (x-value). If the vertical line crosses the graph at exactly one point each time, the relation is a function. In this article, we will explore what the vertical line test is, how to apply it and solve some examples based on it.

What is the Vertical Line Test?

The vertical line test states that a curve represents a function if and only if any vertical line intersects the curve at exactly one point. A vertical line is defined as a line perpendicular to the x-axis.

The intersection of a vertical line and the curve represents the solution at that particular value of the input (x). If the line intersects the curve at more than one point, it means that the curve has more than one output for that value of x, which violates the definition of a function, where each input (x) must correspond to exactly one output (y).

How Does the Vertical Line Test Work?

To use vertical line test, we can use the following steps:

  • Imagine drawing vertical lines (parallel to the y-axis) across the graph.
  • If any vertical line crosses the graph more than once, the graph does not represent a function.
  • If every vertical line touches the graph at most once, then the graph does represent a function.

Why is the Vertical Line Test Important?

This test helps confirm whether a relation (a set of ordered pairs) is a function, where each input (x-value) has exactly one output (y-value).

For example:

  • A parabola (y = x²) passes the Vertical Line Test, so it represents a function.
  • A circle (x² + y² = r²) fails the Vertical Line Test because a vertical line can intersect it at two points, so it does not represent a function.

Applications of the Vertical Line Test

The applications of the Vertical Line Test are as follows:

  • Graphical Analysis: It helps in analyzing the behavior of different functions and their graphs.
  • Curve Sketching: It helps determine whether a given curve sketch represents a function.

Practice Problems on Vertical Line Test

Problem 1: Examine the graph of the relation y = |x|. Does it pass the Vertical Line Test?

Problem 2: Given the graph of a circle with the equation x2 + y2 = 25, determine if the graph represents a function using the Vertical Line Test.

Problem 3: Consider the graph of y = x3. Apply the Vertical Line Test to check if it is a function.

Problem 4: Look at the graph of the equation y=±√x​. Does this relation pass the Vertical Line Test?

Problem 5: For the graph of the equation y=1/x​, test if it satisfies the Vertical Line Test.

Problem 6: Use the Vertical Line Test on the graph of y = sin⁡(x). Does this graph represent a function?

Problem 7: Evaluate the graph of x = y2 + 3 using the Vertical Line Test. Is this graph a function?

Problem 8: Given a straight line graph of y = 3x + 2, determine if it passes the Vertical Line Test.

Problem 9: Look at the graph of the relation y = x2/4 + 2. Can it pass the Vertical Line Test?

Problem 10: Examine the graph of a horizontal line y = 5. Does this line pass the Vertical Line Test?

Answer Key

  • The graph of y = ∣x∣ passes the Vertical Line Test. It is a function.
  • The graph of the circle x2 + y2 = 25 fails the Vertical Line Test. It is not a function.
  • The graph of y = x3 passes the Vertical Line Test. It is a function.
  • The graph of y = ±√x​ fails the Vertical Line Test. It is not a function.
  • The graph of y = 1/x passes the Vertical Line Test. It is a function.
  • The graph of y = sin⁡(x) passes the Vertical Line Test. It is a function.
  • The graph of x = y2 + 3 fails the Vertical Line Test. It is not a function.
  • The graph of y = 3x + 2 passes the Vertical Line Test. It is a function.
  • The graph of y = x2/4+2 passes the Vertical Line Test. It is a function.
  • The graph of the horizontal line y = 5 passes the Vertical Line Test. It is a function.

Conclusion

In this article, we learned about the Vertical Line Test, what it is, how to apply it, and its importance. We also solved some examples of identifying functions using the Vertical Line Test. By mastering this test, we can accurately determine if an expression or graph represents a function, which helps in gaining a clearer understanding of functional relationships.
